newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurofighter partner sees no delay in production.
newsitem.headline: Eurofighter partner sees no delay in production.

text.p: The British partner in the four-nation Eurofighter jet said on Saturday that it can still be produced on time for first delivery to Britain's Royal Air Force in 2001 if German delays to the project can be overcome this year.
British Aerospace Plc joint managing director John Weston told a news briefing at the Paris air show that the flight test programme was running according to plan.
He said the four industrial partners have been working behind the scenes getting ready for production while Germany deliberates.
"Eurofighter is ready for production...we hope by the end of the year we will have the (production) contract in place," he said.

Weston told Reuters later: "The partners have been working at their own risk in lining up production and if the Germans do what they have said they will do, we can still be on schedule for first delivery in 2001."

The future of the 40 billion pound ($65.5 billion) project has been put in doubt by political wrangling in Bonn over whether Germany can afford to buy 180 aircraft as its share of the production run. Britain has already agreed to buy 232 of the aircraft with Italy and Spain taking the balance.
The industrial partners had hoped to get government approvals at the end of last year in order to get first deliveries by the year 2001, in time for first service in 2003.
Germany still has to give its backing but Chancellor Helmut Kohl told Britain earlier this month he hoped a decision would be made in a few weeks.
Weston also said that customer governments now have a "ceiling price" for the 620 aircraft due to be produced for the four nations -- Britain, Germany, Italy and Spain.
Eurofighter is being developed by BAe, Daimler-Benz unit Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Finmeccanica of Italy's Alenia, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa) of Spain. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
